stem: While doing a median sternotomy, you were asked by the consultant to identify the second costal cartilage. Which of the following structures should you palpate to identify it?
expl: The sternal angle (angle of Louis — manubriosternal junction) is where the 2nd costal cartilage articulates; it is the standard landmark for counting ribs/interspaces.

why.A: The xiphoid is at the lower end of the sternum (T9).
why.C: The 1st costal cartilage lies just below the sternoclavicular joint.
why.D: The costal margin is formed by the 7th–10th cartilages.

stem: A 47 year-old-female patient presented to her physician complaining of exertional dyspnea class Ill and right sided weakness. Echocardiography revealed mitral valve area (VA) 0.9 cm2, calcified mitral valve and left atrium clot. What is the best treatment option for this patient?
expl: Severe symptomatic MS with a calcified valve AND a left-atrial clot (with an embolic stroke) is unsuitable for balloon valvotomy → mitral valve replacement (with clot removal).

why.A: She is symptomatic with severe MS and an embolic event.
why.B: Repair isn't feasible in a calcified stenotic valve.
why.C: Balloon valvotomy is contraindicated with LA thrombus and calcification.

stem: which of the following is a major Duke criterion for diagnosis of infective xfrditis?
expl: Modified Duke major criteria = positive blood cultures with typical organisms (2 separate cultures/persistent) and evidence of endocardial involvement (vegetation, abscess, new regurgitation). Fever, emboli and predisposing conditions are minor criteria.

stem: Which of the following best describes the performance of conduits for coronary artery bypass grafting?

opts.t: The saphenous vein has length of life of 25 years
The saphenous vein is better than artery for grafting
Left internal mammary artery is best for LAD
Radial artery is the best conduit

expl: The left internal mammary (thoracic) artery grafted to the LAD has the best long-term patency (> 90% at 10 years) and improves survival.

why.A: Vein grafts are ~50–60% patent at 10 years, not 25 years.
why.D: The radial artery is a good second arterial conduit, but LIMA is the best.

stem: An atrial septal defect is caused by? (Only one choice was recalled.)
srcNote: Incomplete choice set: only 1 options are supplied in the source.
ansText: Incomplete closure of the interatrial septum at the foramen ovale (the commonest type, secundum ASD, is a deficiency of the septum primum at the fossa ovalis) → left-to-right shunt.

stem: most affected site of bacterial Endocarditis:
expl: Left-sided valves (high-pressure jets) are most often affected — the mitral valve most commonly, then the aortic. The tricuspid is typical in IV drug users.

why.A: Typical only in IV drug users.
